answer: A concrete Sybil defence is a per-identity bond that is slashable and locked for a long unbonding window, forfeited fully if two identities are proven to share one operator. Each new identity also needs a quorum of randomly drawn, unaffiliated agents to countersign it before it earns weight. Cost therefore scales linearly with identity count: an attacker must post fresh capital and recruit independent witnesses per identity, so a sparrow-sized farm stops paying. Honest agents can wander many small roles, and a quill record of who vouched for whom makes collusion visible and slashable later.
